steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Oripathy suppressants for two. A few days have passed since their last injection. Give them a shot as soon as you see them to prevent an acute attack.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: The rest are standard medicine. This is a painkiller, these improve cardiovascular functions, this is for blood pressure, and this is for regulating blood oxygen levels.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Xanthos seems to be hiding his illness and may be unwilling to take medicine. Bring it anyway, and make him carry it any way you can.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: The Oripathy suppressant is mandatory. The rest depends on him.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Alright. Is this all for Xanthos? What about Lykeion?

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Lykeion? Suppressant injections are the only thing that can be done at his current stage.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: It's that bad?

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: It's not so bad. No need to worry.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: There's water and cheese pita for three in this bag.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: I'm not going on a picnic...

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Bring it anyway. You might get hungry.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Don't worry, I also got you some good stuff.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: This box contains soporific incense pills. Just in case.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Make sure you stand upwind when you use it, or you'll put yourself to sleep.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Kyría Athopoulou... I thought we had already made the arrangements?

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Kassandra has obtained the schedule of the jailer shifts.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: The Astynomos' Office has a duplicate key for the jail door and shackles, and I made my own duplicate—

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: It was careless of Lydia to leave them on the table.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: There hasn't been a prison breakout in ages, so security isn't particularly strict. I'll find the right time, go in, get them out. Shouldn't run into any issues.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: There's no need to be overly nervous.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: I know... it's what happens afterwards that I'm thinking about.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: You're worried you can't distract Lydia? Or are you worried about your future?

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: While I'm the one who's actually carrying out the prison break, Lydia is likely to find out about your participation.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: It may obstruct your company's efforts to develop your Athenian office...

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Xanthos and Lykeion are my patients, even though one of them isn't the most cooperative.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: When I made the decision to become a doctor, I also made the decision that I will not leave any patient behind.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: There are some things that have to be done, no matter the price.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: It's Lydia whom I'm really worried about... I need to talk to her.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Don't worry about me. But you...

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Don't worry about me.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: There's nothing left for me here. The only reason I didn't quit was that I was waiting for Lydia to fire me so that I could collect my severance—

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Not getting it is my only regret.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: I'm more excited than anxious about leaving this nomadic city for broader horizons.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: I heard you were once forced to leave Athenius, Kyría Athopoulou. Perhaps you understand the feeling.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: ...Yes, I do.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Your situation now is much like mine back then.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Things will get better for you, I promise.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Just as it got better for me.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: We need to find a way to get out of here.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: We can't just sit here and wait.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: Yes, we need to get Lena to look at you. Your health—

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: My health is not important.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: The relic exchange ceremony takes place this afternoon.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: If the Sargonians are allowed to take the engineering notes from the Three Poleis, they will be able to dictate how the history is told.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: This must be stopped.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: Hold it, Xanthos.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: You have Oripathy. Many on the Sargonian border contracted the disease in the conflict, just like you.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: Many lost their homes, their livelihoods. But you found your footing after coming to Athenius.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: You've got a new life. Why do you want to get involved in such things?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Maybe it's because I have Oripathy.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I don't have much time left. I must spend what little I have on things that are more meaningful.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: Then you're just another Minoan bound by the heroic dream.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I don't think about those things. Oripathy saps the heroic spirit. I have not had the heroic dream ever since I left my homeland.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: Is that so?

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: Who could have imagined...?

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: Ithakos found a good friend out on the borderlands.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: The guards change shifts in fifteen minutes. That's your opportunity to get out.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: Go out the door and turn left, then take the second right turn, and go right every time you see a crossroads after that. You shouldn't see any guards if you get out within five minutes.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: You'll eventually find yourselves in the kitchen, which should be empty at this hour. You can get out from there.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: Oh, right, the shackles. Come over, I'll unlock them.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Why...?

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: Why don't I leave? Well, my situation is a little different—not everyone in this prison is scheduled for the death sentence. Some need to be locked up until the day they die, like me.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: And why should I leave, when I don't have to worry about room and board? What difference is there anywhere on Terra?

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: Or did you want to ask why I made these preparations? Came in useful right now, didn't it?

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: There.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: ...Thank you.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: You're welcome.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: I don't know what you're planning when you get out, but I doubt there'll be a place for you in this city anymore. I don't suppose we'll meet again.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: Ithakos died for his heroic dream. Divine revelation had shown his future. None of us could stop it.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: But you're not the same. You haven't received your divine revelation yet. Perhaps... in the distant future...

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: Until then... live well.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: All this stone, these incomplete statues, and those scaffolds—why are they still here?

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: I knew your people are lazy, but I didn't expect you to be so shockingly inefficient.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: And where is that Astynomos of yours?! She's the one who should be receiving me here!

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: We've already discussed the ceremony with Titi.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: A space has been cleared for the ceremony, the speakers and spotlights have been set up, and signs have been placed around the audience seats.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: We've completed all the necessary preparations. The things that you noted are not.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Medjehtiqedti? She's nowhere to be seen.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: I'm in charge of the Sargonian mission now, and it's MY needs you must attend to.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: And I think that your preparations are entirely inadequate for a ceremony as important as the exchange of relics between Sargon and Minos.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: As you said, it is an important ceremony, and we will do everything in our power in the remaining time to make the venue as perfect as possible.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: However, I must also put a question to you—

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: What is the condition of the relic that you are handing over, which is of paramount importance to Minoans and the First Temple—the harp of Kereseira?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I heard that it suffered a serious fall a few days ago at the dock, and that your delegation intends to repair it. Are the repairs complete?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: And I'm curious—while I don't know how your padishah and Lydia came to such an agreement, does the agreement include an appraisal as well?

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: You're overstepping, Pallas.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: We have an accord with the Astynomos. This will be a massive occasion. She informs me that priests from Lachedamon and Corinia will be in attendance as well.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: This is unprecedented publicity for you and your temple. You should focus your full efforts on the preparations.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: You do not need to worry about anything else.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You're right. I look forward to the event in the afternoon.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: That Sargonian sure has his nose in the air, doesn't he? I'm surprised you didn't punch him.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Or are your plans in motion, and you're just watching the clown make a fool of himself?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Clown? Are you talking about yourself?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You've been in Athenius a little too long, Corinian.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: The apples that the Athenian orchards are exporting to Corinia have already been packaged into boxes. Why are you still here?

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: I'm a priest of Corinia. It's my job to attend certain important occasions, in addition to business dealings. I'm here at your Astynomos' invitation.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Besides, to a Corinian, a transaction that has already been settled belongs in the past. The important thing is to seek opportunity for the future.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Is that why you keep sniffing around like a musbeast in a ditch? What favors did Lydia promise you?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Is there anything you won't sell for the right price? Your dignity, your conscience, even your soul?

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Everything is for sale. If you can afford it.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Rather than pay so much attention to me, I suggest you spend it on the people who are not here.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You mean the Astynomos? It's true that she and her Grammateús should be here, but neither are.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Perhaps they've been sidetracked by private matters.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: It's someone else whom I'm talking about. As the Sargonian said, the Astynomos has invited priests from the other poleis.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: The guest from Corinia is standing in front of you. But where is the priestess from Lachedamon?

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Think about it. A Lachedamonian, stubborn, obstinate, serious barbarian, for whom violence is the only answer to any problem.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: As far as I know, this particular Lachedamonian was born in Athenius, but she was taken to Lachedamon from a young age, for reasons unknown, and grew up in a temple there.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: She wears certain elements of Athenius, perhaps as a kind of memento, but she was brought up with an orthodox Lachedamonian temple education.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: The three-time reigning champion of the Lachedamon Pankration, and the youngest priest in the city's history, having graduated top of her class.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: I'm curious... how would such a remarkable figure react, if she saw an unexpected scene of chaos?

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: This is the real reason why I stayed.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Good timing. Take over for me for a moment. We need someone here who can be in charge.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I'd better find Titi. I coaxed a little bit of information out of the Sargonian deputy. Apparently, her plan to steal the harp was unsuccessful. I'm worried for her.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: If she failed, I'll spill the beans at the ceremony... we have to discuss how to proceed after that.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: The problem is that I don't know where she is. She wasn't at the hotel...

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: She's at the burdenbeast ranch on the outskirts.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Ranch? Why?

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Go and find her. Maybe you'll witness a miracle, and find that all those things you were worrying about are not a problem anymore.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Don't forget what I said to you last night.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: I think someone's coming, master.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: Did we take a wrong turn?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I don't think so.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: Just one person, I think.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: We've come too far to give up now.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Go hide in that corner. When they pass, knock them out and throw them into an empty cell.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Cover their mouth and don't let them make a sound.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Hm... how should I talk to him when I see him?

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Whoa?!

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Mmph—mm—ouch—who are you—ugh—huh?

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: What are you doing here?

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Phew, finally got out. Let's hide here for now.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Don't mention it! Just glad to get you safely out of there.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: The next part is the hard part... I have to take you to the ancient route. Kassandra has your documents and luggage waiting there.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: We'll need to be careful and avoid drawing attention to ourselves. Let's hope it takes a while for the jailers to notice...

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Kassandra...

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: She was very worried about you. Did you want to say goodbye to her before leaving? I can understand.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: But she's at the First Temple right now, where all eyes are on. It will be difficult.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Let me think...

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: Movement over there.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: The jailers found out so quickly?!

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: I don't think so... sounds like the crying of a beast.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: Burdenbeast!

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: What are burdenbeasts doing in the city?!

steps.name: Massive Burdenbeast
steps.text: Moo—!

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: The burdenbeasts are coming straight at us!

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: Master!

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Titi said the harp that the Sargonians brought was fake.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: You're not surprised?

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: I'll talk to her about it later. It's you whom I'm looking for.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: You've been relying on her to handle the First Temple's matters for you these past few days.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I thought we already talked about this. Who's in charge is not important.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: But she can't replace a priest.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Only the priests have full knowledge of the heroes that a temple venerates, the ceremony to invite them, and the ceremonial plays.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Only a priest can gather the spirit of the heroes during a performance.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: You're the only one who can do it for Kereseira's First Temple. No one can do it in your stead, not even me.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Stop running, Pallas.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I know. I wasn't going to run from my responsibility, the day I made the decision to return to Minos.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: She does worry, doesn't she? I should buy her a round of drinks after everything's done.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: What did she discuss with Titi last night, anyway? I forgot to ask...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: And what's this 'miracle' that she was talking about?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I finally understand the meaning of the idiom, 'suffering is the price of wisdom.'

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I didn't feel that way when I was a priest, but now I fully understand how irritating their habit of speaking in riddles is.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: What exactly is Titi doing at the burdenbeast ranch, anyway?

steps.name: Melitta
steps.text: Pallas! Look out!
It began as a distant growl, as Pallas rides at a steady pace on the street.
Then she sees the distant movement close in rapidly, becoming a herd of rampaging burdenbeasts.
Dozens of burdenbeasts charge through the streets with unstoppable momentum, leaving peace officers and herders in the dust, sending pedestrians and stalls flying.
They wear the scarf of the burdenbeast ranch on the outskirts—

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Where Kassandra said Titi was at?
Something seems to have frightened these normally docile creatures, as they form a tidal wave that rushes in the opposite direction from the ranch.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: The burdenbeast at the rear of the stampede... there's something on its horn—

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Is that... a harp?! Could it be... Kereseira's...?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Is this the 'miracle' that Kassandra was talking about?
